newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Telstra's Blount happy with current sale plan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Telstra's Blount happy with current sale plan.

text.p: Telstra Corp chief executive Frank Blount said he would not get involved in the political controversy about the company's future, but was happy with plans to privatise one third of the state-owned telecommunications carrier during the current term of the national parliament.
"The real benefit comes with the first tranche, it really does," Blount told reporters.
"Now whether or not it goes further, I would say 89 percent of the benefit has already been captured."
Communications Minister Richard Alston said on the weekend that all of Telstra could be eventually sold.
Blount said the possible sale of more than has already been announced by the government, subject to approval in the upper house of parliament, "almost becomes irrelevant to me".
"It is the policymakers who have to make up their mind on that and the Australian people. It really is their decision not mine."

Alston's comments sparked criticism from the opposition Labor Party and key minority members of the Senate about the government's true plan for Telstra and a rebuke from Prime Minister John Howard who said policy had not been changed and only a one-third privatisation was planned.

"I am trying to run a telephone company and I am leaving the policy issues up to the government and the minister of the day, Senator Alston," Blount said after addressing a lunch meeting of the Securities Institute of Australia.

He told the meeting that the partial sale, expected to raise about A$8 billion, had been supported by most brokers who hoped for some business but oneeanalyst argued it could not succeed unless the foreign ownership restriction of 30 percent was increased. Blount did not agree, saying the sale would include a share offer to employees. "We don't think it is going to be a problem," he said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
